question_text:
The magnetization within a bar of some metal alloy is $1.2 \times 10^{6} \mathrm{~A} / \mathrm{m}$ at an H field of $200 \mathrm{~A} / \mathrm{m}$. Compute the following: (a) the magnetic susceptibility, (b) the permeability, and (c) the magnetic flux density within this material. 

Give your answer as a tuple (the magnetic susceptibility, the permeability, the magnetic flux density).The units of each required answer are (, H/m, tesla), respectively.
response:
## Solution

**Given:** $M = 1.2\times10^{6}\,\text{A/m}$, $H = 200\,\text{A/m}$, $\mu_0 = 4\pi\times10^{-7}\,\text{H/m}$

**(a) Magnetic susceptibility:**
$$\chi_m = \frac{M}{H} = \frac{1.2\times10^{6}}{200} = 6000$$

**(b) Permeability:**
$$\mu = \mu_0(1+\chi_m) = 4\pi\times10^{-7}\times(6001) \approx 7.54\times10^{-3}\,\text{H/m}$$

**(c) Magnetic flux density:**
$$B = \mu H = \mu_0(H+M) \approx 1.508\,\text{T}$$

$$\boxed{(6000,\ 0.00754,\ 1.508)}$$
